paraphrase: Most inscriptions are read right to left; seals and impressions require distinguishing the mirrored face.

paraphrase: Patterned texts have recurring ordered fields; complex texts contain more variable, language-like sequences.

paraphrase: He distinguishes transcriptive writing from notational writing and treats both as present in Indus texts.

paraphrase: Reading-order fields are P, M, C and T, with optional omissions. P is a position label rather than a grammatical prefix.

paraphrase: M fields contain an oval subfield, a fish subfield and a mortar/pestle-plus-three-strokes subfield.

paraphrase: Within a complete M field, the reading order is oval, fish, MS.

paraphrase: The fish subfield uses seven entries, has at most three entries and does not repeat an entry.

paraphrase: The oval subfield uses three entries and has ordering restrictions comparable to fish.

paraphrase: The MS construction strongly associates the mortar/pestle-like sign with three long strokes.

paraphrase: Jar and arrow signs function as terminal-field signs and can accompany other fields.

paraphrase: Short ticks and paired bars delimit parts of patterned inscriptions and express a case-like relationship.
